reasoning: The popular adage "Lightning never strikes the same place twice" is scientifically false. According to the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) and the National Weather Service (NWS), lightning frequently strikes the same location multiple times, particularly tall, pointed, and isolated structures that offer a path of least resistance for electrical discharges. A prime example is the Empire State Building in New York City, which is struck by lightning an average of 25 times every year.
